summary: Host Alien claimed the MB-003 migration stage. Digital-City claim commit 5e69ebf0e366835547eb3c36e596937fe58565ec pushed to City main with no write conflict. MB-001 migration is COMPLETE and MB-002 migration is held by host Mech, so MB-003 is the lowest-sequence claimable migration. Branch mission/MB-003-worker-gateway created from utopia main c7ef3cd1c6be0155332d03afc3607dfdbf49c205.

Reconnaissance started. Target is the EXISTING building city/02-engineering/02-worker-gateway, which already owns the migrated skill-intake module, so MB-003 must land as a NEW sibling module in that building (skill-intake must not be forked). Donors are DS-Hns @ eeb57ca (worker/task contract, provider adapter, readiness/health) and Codex-Boss @ 8df428e (provider session/router/circuit-breaker/outcome). A third donor clone at the DS-Hns frozen SHA is required before any boundary decision.

Landed three new modules in the EXISTING city/02-engineering/02-worker-gateway building (skill-intake untouched): worker-task-contract (DS-Hns scheduler/lifecycle.js, 23 tests), provider-adapter (Codex-Boss runtimes/runtime.ts + unsupported-runtime.ts + web/provider-runtime-adapter.ts + src/shared/provider-state.ts, 29 tests), provider-resilience (Codex-Boss commander/circuit-breaker.ts + src/shared/provider-outcome.ts, 42 tests). Extended city/CITY_IMPLEMENTATION_MANIFEST.json and the census test; added the mission-incubation provenance contract; documented all of it bilingually in city/docs.

Two real failures. (1) Adding three unbridged modules made the capability registry advertise them to Web and Android as unavailable capabilities, which broke the existing capability-registry and capability-adapters count assertions. (2) My first attempt to consume the migrated breaker called the standalone exported accessors state(breaker,id)/observeFailure(breaker,id); those take a snapshot core, not the object createCircuitBreaker returns, so the bridge threw TypeError on every request. The module's bound methods are the stateful API. A third, self-inflicted failure was caught before commit in the same module family's test expectations.

Repairs. (1) Rather than editing the count assertions, a module-level capabilityProvider flag was added: the three adapter-infrastructure modules declare capabilityProvider:false and the capability registry skips them, so the product capability surface returns to exactly its pre-MB-003 shape and the pre-existing assertions pass untouched. The flag is validated in city/manifest.mjs. (2) The bridge now uses the breaker's bound methods (circuit.state(id), circuit.observeFailure(id)). A new test proves the bridge refuses exactly what the Core refuses, and that a capability-wide EXECUTION_TIMEOUT - a failure, but not a provider-health signal - still must not degrade anything. No assertion was deleted, skipped or weakened.

Full CI-equivalent suite green: pnpm test 59/59, apps/rooms tests 67/67, city/test-all.mjs 224/224, verify-promotion-history.mjs 10 records verified, check:docs SYNCHRONIZED in docs, evidence and data-records. New module tests: worker-task-contract 23, provider-adapter 29, provider-resilience 42 (94 total).

Real consumption verified: services/capability-bridge/bridge.mjs now decides per-capability degradation through the migrated provider-resilience breaker, with Utopia's policy (failureThreshold 1, cooldown 604800000, and only ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE / ADAPTER_UNAVAILABLE counting) supplied as data. tests/capability-bridge.test.mjs drives a real bridge over a real Store: a timeout leaves the capability AVAILABLE, a provider-technical failure degrades it, the Core reaches the same verdict for the same policy, further work is refused with BRIDGE_PENDING, and unrelated capabilities are unaffected. Behaviour is identical to the ad-hoc Set it replaced: a degraded capability is refused before dispatch, so no success is ever observed and nothing ever closes the breaker.

Hosted required CI green for the implementation SHA aff3c283e34b596c6c0ba6c666aed96893b6c395: V0.2 checks run 36570163616 completed success. The claim-stage push 590d041c4398c11f53dce9c821a2c0c44d508edd also ran green under run 36567419904. Local CI-equivalent results on the same tree: pnpm test 59/59, apps/rooms 67/67, city/test-all.mjs 224/224, verify-promotion-history 10 records, check:docs SYNCHRONIZED, Android :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:assembleDebug BUILD SUCCESSFUL (all tasks up-to-date; apps/android unchanged).

MB-003 migration stage complete on host Alien. Three modules landed beside the untouched skill-intake in city/02-engineering/02-worker-gateway: worker-task-contract (DS-Hns), provider-adapter and provider-resilience (Codex-Boss), 94 parity tests. Real consumption: the capability bridge's per-capability degradation decision is owned by the migrated provider-resilience breaker with Utopia's policy supplied as data, exactly equivalent to the ad-hoc Set it replaced. Recorded boundaries, not hidden: two of three modules have no product consumer; circuit-breaker persistence is deferred; DS-Hns's real adapter plane in app/core/plugin-adapters, app/sub-worker and app/engineering was not migrated; and MB-001/MB-003 will conflict at merge time over the manifest, the census test and the bilingual docs. Branch not merged and mission:finalize not run, per the mission-book. City report: Digital-City/mission-book/reports/MB-003/MIGRATION_REPORT.md.
